author: Marlon Chaviano
name: saas-django
title: SaaS with Django
description: Django for a SaaS: accounts with django-allauth (sign-up, email login and password reset), admin, ORM and tests, with optional Postgres and Sentry.

base.command: mkdir {{name}} && cd {{name}} && python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -q django django-allauth && .venv/bin/django-admin startproject config .

writeFiles.content:
# --- Accounts with django-allauth (first-commit) ---
INSTALLED_APPS += ["allauth", "allauth.account"]
MIDDLEWARE += ["allauth.account.middleware.AccountMiddleware"]
AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS = [
    "django.contrib.auth.backends.ModelBackend",
    "allauth.account.auth_backends.AuthenticationBackend",
]
ACCOUNT_LOGIN_METHODS = {"email"}
ACCOUNT_SIGNUP_FIELDS = ["email*", "password1*", "password2*"]
LOGIN_REDIRECT_URL = "/"

from django.urls import include  # noqa: E402

urlpatterns += [path("accounts/", include("allauth.urls"))]

verify.command: .venv/bin/python manage.py check && .venv/bin/python manage.py migrate --noinput && .venv/bin/python manage.py test && (test ! -f pytest.ini || .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q)

instructions:
## How to work here

- Accounts come from django-allauth (`/accounts/login/`, `/accounts/signup/`); customize its templates by copying them into `templates/account/`, don't edit the package.
- Protect views with `@login_required` (or `LoginRequiredMixin`) and check on the server that each object belongs to the user.
- Organize by domain apps (`python manage.py startapp <name>`); model changes always through `makemigrations`.
- Before finishing: `manage.py check && manage.py test`.
